summary: The article describes how schools in the Local Education Systems have combined environmental science with physical education since September 2023. It profiles ten activities, from the Green Marathon and Wildlife Workout to Climate Change Tag and The Expedition Challenge, each led by a named teacher or school. All use movement and games to teach conservation, recycling, renewable energy and ecosystems.
one_line: Ten eco-themed physical education activities introduced in schools since September 2023 teach environmental science through movement, games and outdoor challenges.
key_facts: Mike "Marathon" Johnson, PE teacher at Springfield Elementary, introduced the Green Marathon on October 10, 2023, a fun run with environmental science stations on local flora and fauna, renewable energy, and recycling.
Diane Rivers of Cedar High unveiled the Wildlife Workout on September 15, 2023, in which students mimic animals by hopping like frogs, sprinting like cheetahs and balancing like flamingos.

Oakwood Junior High's Eco Obstacle Courses, reported on November 5, 2023, have sections representing deforestation or pollution, such as climbing a 'mountain' of recycled materials or crawling through a 'forest' of saplings.
John Beaumont of Valley Middle School introduced the Recycling Relay on September 29, 2023, in which students sort recyclables into plastic, glass and paper bins and pass items to teammates.
Kelly Simons led Plant-a-Plot Pilates on September 21, 2023, at Greenwood Park, combining Pilates with gardening; students planted herbs and flowers and learned about plant life cycles.

Coach Robert Delaney of Pines Elementary introduced Climate Change Tag on December 1, 2023, where 'It' represents carbon emissions and tagged students unfreeze when classmates perform an eco-friendly action.
Emily Hartwell of Solar Springs High School unveiled Solar-Powered Circuit Training on September 20, 2023, using stations with solar-powered timers and equipment plus facts about solar power.
Geography teacher Stephen Frank led students in the Quest for Clean-Up on October 13, 2023, jogging through local parks while picking up trash.
Brookfield Elementary debuted Biome Bingo in November 2023; students do biome-linked exercises, such as sprints for deserts and agility moves for rainforests, to mark off bingo cards.
The Lionsgate High School orienteering team began The Expedition Challenge on October 25, 2023, navigating by map and compass to checkpoints that teach about local conservation efforts.
The article says the trend has been seen in the Local Education Systems since September 2023 and signals a paradigm shift blending health and environmental education.
